I am an old woman, 76 years, and this small piece of land is not even mine — I rent it. My cassava and cocoyam I plant like my mother taught me, with the cuttings I saved from last year. I have no money for the fertilizer from the shop, and my neighbors here do not put it on their cassava anyway — we just clear the bush, heap the soil, and plant. My children help me small-small when they can, but most of the work I do myself slowly, slowly.
